question.leadin: This outspoken critic of the death penalty executed thousands of political opponents during his reign of power on the Committee of Public Safety.
question.text: Name this "public accuser" who promoted the Cult of the Supreme Being and guillotined [GEE-uh-teen'd] supporters of the monarchy during the "Reign of Terror."
question.answerHtml: Maximilien Robespierre [“robes”-p’yair] (or Maximilien François Marie Isidore de Robespierre )
question.clue: This leader promoted the Cult of the Supreme Being and secured power after the death of his former ally Georges Danton.

swap.text: This politician and general opposed the Vichy government, instead leading Free France during World War II. He later established the Fifth Republic in France.
swap.answerHtml: Charles de Gaulle (accept Charles Andr´e Joseph Marie de Gaulle)
swap.clue: This president faced a wildcat strike in May 1968 and incurred the wrath of the OAS by signing the Evian accords.

question.text: At this 1415 victory for England's Henry V, longbowmen and wooden stakes halted the French cavalry charge across a muddy battlefield.
question.clue: It also saw Thomas Erpingham led one side after his earlier siege of Harfleur.

swap.leadin: Cardinal Richelieu besieged members of this group at La Rochelle. --.
swap.text: Name this religious group whose freedom of worship was granted by the Edict of Nantes and revoked by the Edict of Fontainebleau.
swap.clue: These people were welcomed into Prussia via the Edict of Potsdam.

question.text: This French Emperor was captured at Sedan. He shares his name with a more famous uncle.
question.clue: Together with Camilo Cavour, this man concluded the secret agreement of Plombiers, and assistance to the Piedmontese in the victory over Austria at the Battle of Solferino resulted in the Peace of Villafranca.

swap.leadin: A group of probably fictitious female arsonists during this government were known as the petroleuse (PET-roh-looz).
swap.text: Name this socialist regime that controlled a national capital before being crushed by the Third Republic under Adolphe Thiers (teerz) in 1871.
swap.clue: The Hˆotel de Ville, Tuileries and Louvre library were destroyed by arson during this event, which was opposed by Adolphe Thiers .

question.leadin: This dynasty's king Clovis defeated a Roman rump state under Syagrius at the Battle of Soissons in 486 CE.
question.text: Name this dynasty founded by Childeric I. The Salic Law was first codified under this dynasty.
question.clue: These kings all had long hair and gave power to regional "mayors of the palace" after Dagobert I's rule.

swap.text: After Richelieu's death, the French nobility, allied with peasants and other factions, engaged in two rebellions against the monarchy collectively given this name. It is French for "sling," which rebels used to smash windows.
swap.clue: That council led by Anne of Austria was challenged by the victor at Lens, who led the second stage of this uprising and briefly occupied Paris with Spanish help.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a leader per part.
question.text: Known as "The Hammer," this grandfather of Charlemagne won victories over Muslim and Saxon armies.
question.clue: He served as Mayor of the Palace in Austrasia, a title he passed to his son, Pepin III after securing another victory at the Battle of Cologne.

swap.text: The wife of this man, the successor to Charles de Gaulle after interim president Alain Poher, was involved in the Markovic Affair.
swap.clue: He convinced de Gaulle to adopt key reforms that diffused the student strikes of 1968.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the American African offensive in World War II.
question.text: Eisenhower made a deal with this notorious Nazi collaborator which allowed him to bypass fighting the Vichy forces and move his troops east towards Rommel's Afrika Korps.

swap.text: The Paris Commune that formed after the war was suppressed by this French leader, who then founded the Third Republic and served as the first president from 1871-1873.
swap.clue: This prime minister sparked the Rhine Crisis by declaring the river was the "natural eastern border" of France. As the first president of the Third Republic, he ordered Patrice MacMahon to crush the Paris Commune.

question.leadin: This ruler legendarily ordered his first wife, Elisabeth of Vendome, to be burnt at the stake over accusations of adultery.
question.text: Name this early count of Anjou who pioneered a strategy of coupling territorial expansion with the creation of an extensive network of defensive fortifications, monasteries, and abbeys.
question.answerHtml: Fulk Nerra [or Fulk III of Anjou or Foulque Nerra or Fulk the Black; prompt on Fulk of Anjou or Nerra alone]

swap.text: French religious freedom took a hit during this 1572 event, during which Gaspard de Coligny and other Huguenots were attacked.
swap.clue: This event was precipitated by the wedding of Margaret of Valois.

question.leadin: Answer the following on the career of Joseph Gallieni.
question.text: In Madagascar, Gallieni commanded this officer who later served ahead of Gallieni as Commander-in-Chief of French Forces on the Western Front until 1916.
question.clue: As chief of staff, he adopted Plan 17 as the main strategy for defending France from Germany in World War I. He was later replaced by Robert Nivelle and promoted to Marshal of France.

swap.text: Early vassalage ceremonies involved Christian relics, including those of this saint, the first bishop of Paris who was martyred around 250 CE. After getting beheaded, he picked it up and kept walking for miles, preaching all the way.
swap.answerHtml: Saint Denis [or Dionysius; do not accept "Dionysus the Areopagite"]

question.leadin: This arch-conservative ideology, which formed after the July Revolution, was opposed to republicanism, Bonapartism, and Orleanism.
question.text: Name this political alignment from the July Monarchy onward whose adherents included Honore de Balzac. Partisans of this ideology supported the restoration of the Bourbon dynasty to the French throne.
question.clue: Portions of the Protocols were plagiarized from the Dialogue in Hell Between Machiavelli and Montesquieu, a work by Maurice Joly advancing this royalist position, contrasted with the Orleanists and the Bonapartists.

swap.leadin: This game was derived from an earlier Spanish variety where the dealer distributes a "top layout" and "bottom layout" after all "coups" are revealed.
swap.text: Name this insanely popular confidence game in 1860's Paris that instructed players to "find the lady." Dealers in that game used the "bent corner technique" to trick players who constantly played.

question.leadin: A political cartoon satirized this agreement as "the first kiss this ten years," depicting a thin man kissing an obese woman.
question.text: Name this 1802 agreement between England and France, which brought peace for one year during the otherwise continuous period of fighting between 1793 and 1815. This agreement's breakdown resulted in the formation of the Third Coalition to oppose Napoleon.
question.clue: The Republic of the Seven Ionian Islands achieved recognition as a result of this treaty, and under it Egypt was taken from France and restored to the Ottoman Empire under British supervision.

swap.leadin: Name these historians who wrote on the French Revolution, FTP each.
swap.text: Chair of French Revolutionary history at the Sorbonne from 1937-45, his two-volume The French Revolution ushered in a Marxist approach to the entire era.
